lines.trans: Max, do not hang up, now she really is giving birth!
The most important thing in life is that you must love a woman.
And you must do it with all your heart and fiercely!
Otherwise what kind of real love is it then?
Dasha, forgive me, but I urgently need to get to Moscow!
Tell me, how much does it cost to turn our plane around right now?
That will cost roughly five hundred thousand rubles.
And does your bank issue urgent loans to clients?

words.gloss: to hand out, pass off, betray

lines.trans: Max, do you really still love her that much?
Yes, Dasha, I love her very much!
Alright, sign the papers, we will turn the plane back to Moscow now.

words.gloss: to draw up, to process paperwork

lines.trans: Thank you so much, Vika, just wait for me there!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С этого надо было сразу начинать — тридцать тысяч!
examples.trans: You should have started with that right away—thirty thousand!

examples.text: Тридцать тысяч? Что же ты подавать нам решил?
examples.trans: Thirty thousand? What on earth did you decide to serve us?

examples.text: Это будет стоить примерно пятьсот тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: That will cost roughly five hundred thousand rubles.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rubles' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Макс, не бросай трубку, теперь она и вправду рожает!
examples.trans: Max, do not hang up, now she really is giving birth!

examples.text: Это будет стоить примерно пятьсот тысяч рублей.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Машина красивая, но хозяин очень плохо припарковался.
examples.trans: The car is nice, but the owner parked very badly.

examples.text: Ум за папины деньги точно не купишь!
examples.trans: You certainly cannot buy brains with daddy's money!

examples.text: Женщинам нужны сюрпризы, полные интриги и романтики.
examples.trans: Women need surprises full of intrigue and romance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ваш банк ведь выдаёт клиентам срочные кредиты?
examples.trans: And does your bank issue urgent loans to clients?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Why no, not at all, I am already divorced.

examples.text: Ведь этот белый трюфель — настоящий король деликатесов!
examples.trans: After all, this white truffle is the true king of delicacies!

examples.text: Ведь мой кулинарный шедевр на плите уже готов.
examples.trans: After all, my culinary masterpiece on the stove is already ready.

выдавать.gloss: to hand out, pass off, betray

meanings.en: to pass off (выдавать себя за), hand out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'давать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hand out, pass off, betray'.

examples.text: Он выдавал себя за другого человека.
examples.trans: He passed himself off as another person.

examples.text: Мне правда неловко выдавать себя за писателя.
examples.trans: I really feel awkward impersonating a writer.

meanings.note: From Latin 'cliens' (follower, patron's dependent, customer).

examples.text: А ваш банк ведь выдаёт клиентам срочные кредиты?
examples.trans: And does your bank issue urgent loans to clients?

examples.text: Я сейчас работаю с клиентами.
examples.trans: I'm working with clients right now.

examples.text: Это только для постоянных клиентов.
examples.trans: This is only for regular clients.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('urgent').

examples.text: Мне срочно нужна большая ваза с водой.
examples.trans: I urgently need a large vase with water.

examples.text: Вряд ли получится, у меня внизу срочная работа.
examples.trans: That is unlikely to work out, I have urgent work downstairs.

examples.text: Подожди, мне только что пришло срочное сообщение от Вики!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Скажи честно, Макс, ты сейчас уже женат?
examples.trans: Tell me honestly, Max, are you married now?

examples.trans: Why no, not at all, I am already divorced.

examples.text: Это уже девятнадцатый букет за одну неделю!
examples.trans: This is already the nineteenth bouquet in a single week!

examples.text: Да, они действительно сегодня очень свежие и красивые.
examples.trans: Yes, they really are very fresh and beautiful today.

examples.text: Макс, ты действительно так сильно её ещё любишь?
examples.trans: Max, do you really still love her that much?

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, конечно помню, было такое дело.
examples.trans: Yes, of course I remember, that did happen.

examples.text: Ах, для такого дела? Тогда, конечно, они есть!
examples.trans: Oh, for a cause like that? Then of course I have some!

examples.text: Нет, я до сих пор так никого не встретила.
examples.trans: No, I still have not met anyone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Он сильно запутался в верёвках и приземлился неудачно.
examples.trans: He got badly tangled in the lines and landed poorly.

examples.text: Макс, ты действительно так сильно её ещё любишь?
examples.trans: Max, do you really still love her that much?

examples.text: Да, Даша, я её очень сильно люблю!
examples.trans: Yes, Dasha, I love her very much!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Алло, Даша, твоё предложение насчёт Сочи ещё в силе?
examples.trans: Hello, Dasha, is your offer about Sochi still open?

examples.text: Макс, ты с ума сошёл? Позвони ещё раз!
examples.trans: Max, have you lost your mind? Call them one more time!

examples.text: Ты с ума сошёл? Он же ещё живой!
examples.trans: Have you lost your mind? He is still alive!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Dasha, how glad I am to see you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

оформлять.gloss: to draw up, to process paperwork

meanings.en: to register officially, to process paperwork
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to draw up, to process paperwork', paired with 'оформить'.

related.gloss: not to to draw up (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Хорошо, оформляй бумаги, сейчас развернём самолёт в Москву.

examples.text: Мы согласны, оформляйте!

examples.text: Хорошо, оформляй бумаги, сейчас развернём самолёт в Москву.

дождаться.gloss: to wait for, to live to see

meanings.en: to wait until something happens, to get by waiting (+ genitive)
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ждаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait for, to live to see', paired with 'дожидаться'.

examples.text: Я дождусь ответа.
examples.trans: I will wait for an answer.

examples.text: Я всё равно дождусь твоего ответа!
examples.trans: I will wait for your answer anyway!

examples.text: Я готов спокойно дождаться решения суда.
examples.trans: I am ready to wait calmly for the court decision.
